newsitem.title: USA: Tribune sharpens focus on the Internet.
newsitem.headline: Tribune sharpens focus on the Internet.

text.p: After building itself into a multimedia powerhouse through newspapers, television and radio, Tribune Co is now looking for new ways to grow without abandoning its roots in traditional channels.
"We like the businesses that we're in, but the Internet is where a lot of our focus is currently," said David Hiller, Tribune's senior vice president for development.

Tribune believes the money-making potential of its Internet activities is huge, especially when the cross-over advertising possibilities with its print and broadcasting properties are considered, Hiller said.
"We're less certain when it's going to be huge," Hiller said. "I think people are convinced the Internet is a real medium and a real advertising medium."
The latest communications industry outlook from New York investment banking firm Veronis Suhler & Associates estimates that the Internet could attract up to $2.1 billion in advertising by 2000.
With such high stakes, Tribune has focused on developing capabilities in new media that leverage its expertise as an information provider in traditional channels.

"In 1981-82, when the personal computer first came out, a lot of people were fascinated with it, but it wasn't an 'I-can't-run-my-business-unless-I-have-one' situation," said Jeff Scherb, who last week assumed the newly created position of Tribune senior vice president for technology.
"Now, the Internet is on the verge of the same turning point," he said.
Analysts agree that the importance of the Internet is growing, so an early foothold is important.

"As a preemptive strike, it's a good thing to do," said analyst James Goss of Nesbitt Burns, referring to Tribune's involvement in the emerging medium. Although advertising on the Internet is still in its infancy, competition for supremacy will surely intensify, he said.

Tribune's approach to the new medium will become more evident later this month with the initial rollout of four so-called Digital City electronic "communities," accessible through America Online and the Internet.
The interactive Digital City sites will provide users with local news, entertainment listings and classified advertising.

Tribune will own and operate the Digital City affiliates in areas where it publishes daily newspapers: Chicago (Chicago Tribune), South Florida (Sun-Sentinel), Orlando (Orlando Sentinel) and Hampton Roads, Va. (Daily Press).
Tribune has a 20 percent stake in Digital City Inc and holds five percent of the parent company, America Online Inc.

Tribune also has stakes in Open Market Inc, which develops software for conducting business over the Internet, and CheckFree Corp, which provides banking services through personal computers and the Internet's World Wide Web.

Other properties in which Tribune has a stake include: Excite Inc, an Internet navigation network; SoftKey International Inc, a software publisher; and StarSight Telecast Inc, a developer of interactive television program guides.
